removal.text: Chock the front wheels, raise the rear safely, release the parking brake and remove the wheel.
Unclip the parking-brake cable from its caliper lever and retain its routing. Remove the lower guide fasteners and pivot the caliper clear without straining the hose.
Lift out the pads and inspect the disc, caliper boots, sliding pins and parking-brake mechanism for damage or uneven wear.

installation.text: Clean the pad abutments and caliper contact points. Wind the piston back with the correct tool while monitoring the reservoir level.
installation.warning: Do not force or twist the piston boot; confirm the piston is correctly oriented for the caliper design.

installation.text: Fit the new pads, refit the caliper and apply the specified thread-locking compound to the guide fasteners.
Reconnect the parking-brake cable, check it is fully seated, refit the wheel and tighten the wheel bolts to specification.
Before moving the vehicle, pump the brake pedal until firm and operate the parking brake repeatedly to take up caliper clearance.

checks: Check the brake-fluid level and ensure it is not overfilled after piston retraction.
Confirm a firm pedal, free wheel rotation with the parking brake released, and correct parking-brake operation.
Bed in the pads according to the pad maker's instructions.

faults.causes: Cable not seated, caliper lever binding, or automatic clearance adjustment not reset.
Seized guide pins, sticking piston, or damaged pad abutments.

name: Rear brake disc and integrated bearing

safety: Support the vehicle securely and release the parking brake.
Do not hang the caliper from its hose.
Do not machine brake discs; replace discs with excessive wear or damage.
tools: Jack and axle stands or lift

parts.notes: Replace the disc and pads on both sides of the axle together.

parts.notes: Use new fastening parts if required by the replacement assembly instructions.

installation.text: Clean the hub seating area and install the new disc-and-bearing assembly. Refit the dust cap and carrier using the specified thread-locking compound where called for.
Refit the caliper and wheel; apply the prescribed torques to each fastener and the wheel bolts.
Pump the brake pedal to seat the pads, then cycle the parking brake to confirm automatic adjustment.

Verify no brake-hose twist, correct cable routing, a firm pedal and normal wheel rotation.

Check for leaks, firm pedal travel, and correct parking-brake holding.

name: Brake fluid change and bleeding
summary: Use the specified compatible fluid and pressure-bleeding method. ABS hydraulic-unit bleeding requires a diagnostic tool if the circuit-regulation procedure is triggered.
safety: Brake fluid damages paint and irritates skin; use protective equipment and clean spills promptly.
Keep the reservoir and bleeder equipment supplied with fluid throughout the operation.
Do not drive with a soft or abnormal brake pedal.

removal.text: Confirm the hydraulic and electrical brake-control systems have no faults. Attach the approved pressure bleeder and collection bottles before opening any bleed points.
removal.warning: The standard bleed procedure requires the ignition off so ABS solenoids are not inadvertently activated.

removal.text: Flush each wheel circuit in the specified order, closing each bleed point before moving to the next: rear right, front left, rear left, then front right.
removal.warning: Keep the master-cylinder reservoir and bleeder supply from running dry.

installation.text: If the pedal travel remains abnormal after the base bleed and a road test activates regulation, connect the diagnostic tool and run the ABS hydraulic-unit and circuit bleed routine as directed by the tool.
Disconnect the bleeder, restore the reservoir to the correct level, refit bleed-point caps and inspect for leaks.

checks: With the engine off, verify correct pedal travel; repeat bleeding if necessary.
Road-test cautiously in a safe area and confirm normal braking and pedal feel.
If ABS regulation causes abnormal pedal travel, perform the diagnostic-controlled hydraulic bleed.

faults.causes: Air in the hydraulic circuit, low fluid or a leak; ABS unit may require diagnostic bleeding.
Leak, excessive pad wear or incorrect fluid level.

summary: Remove and refit the front floating caliper without twisting the flexible hose; a hydraulic opening requires bleeding and a level check.

Pump the brake pedal to seat pads before moving the car.

Flare-nut wrench if hose is removed

Restore all retaining clips, bleed the brake circuit and inspect the hose through steering and suspension travel for contact or tension.

Confirm firm pedal feel and full wheel movement without hose contact.

Clear the ABS fault memory and confirm live wheel-speed readings agree during a controlled low-speed check.

Check that the bearing encoder is clean and not damaged.
Confirm the ABS warning lamp goes out and diagnostic data is plausible.

Contamination, excessive sensor gap, damaged encoder or wiring interference.

safety: A compressed coil spring stores lethal energy. Use an inspected, correctly sized spring compressor and follow its instructions.

installation.text: Position the spring ends correctly in their seats and assemble the damper, bearing and mount in the specified order and orientation. Install a new strut-rod nut while the spring remains controlled.

Check that hose and sensor wiring are clipped safely and do not bind through steering movement.

removal.text: Remove the luggage-compartment trim to access the upper mount. Remove its fastener, raise the vehicle and release the lower mount, then remove the damper.

installation.text: Install the damper and loosely fit its lower mount. Position the upper mount correctly, lower the vehicle until the suspension is at normal ride height, then tighten both mounts to specification.

checks: Inspect both dampers for leakage and compare rebound behavior side to side.
Reinstall trim and confirm no hose, cable or suspension part is trapped.

faults.causes: Worn or leaking shock absorber.
Damaged damper bushes or loose mounts.

name: Rear coil spring and spring seats
summary: Rear coil springs sit between the body and rear axle beam, with upper and lower spring seats. Preserve the spring and damper identification markings when selecting replacements.
safety: Support the axle beam with a suitable jack before releasing the shock absorber lower mount.
Never support the vehicle by the rear axle beam.
Replace a dislodged upper spring seat if it no longer clips securely.

parts.name: Rear coil springs
parts.notes: Match the spring identification marks and replace as a pair.

removal.text: Remove the rear wheel and axle protective cover as needed. Support the spring seat with a jack, release the lower damper mount and lower the axle beam in a controlled manner to remove the spring and lower seat.

installation.text: Fit the spring seats and orient each spring to its original position. Raise the axle beam and loosely refit the damper lower mount; final-tighten it only after the wheels are on the ground.

checks: Check spring markings and compare left/right parts before installation.
Confirm each spring end is correctly located and the upper seat is clipped in place.

faults.symptom: Vehicle sits low at one rear corner
faults.causes: Broken or incorrect spring, displaced spring seat or unequal part specification.
Dislodged spring seat, damaged spring or loose damper mount.

name: Rear hub bearing (integrated with brake disc)
summary: The fetched repair data describes the rear wheel bearing as supplied already mounted in the rear brake disc. Replace the disc-and-bearing assembly rather than treating it as a separate press-in rear bearing.
safety: Use a replacement assembly matched to the vehicle and ABS configuration.
Do not damage the bearing encoder or contaminate the brake friction surfaces.
tools: Jack and axle stands or lift

removal.text: Remove the wheel, unclip the parking-brake cable, remove the caliper and carrier, then remove the dust cap and stub-axle nut to withdraw the disc-and-bearing assembly.

installation.text: Install a new integrated disc-bearing assembly, fit the hub nut and dust cap, then reinstall carrier, caliper and parking-brake cable using their applicable procedures.
Pump the brake pedal and cycle the parking brake before driving.

checks: Check bearing play and noise and confirm the ABS encoder remains clean and undamaged.
Inspect the disc and pads as an axle pair.

faults.causes: Worn integrated bearing; replace the rear disc-bearing assembly described by the repair data.

name: Front drive shafts and CV boots
summary: Inspect the inner and outer constant-velocity joint boots for splits, grease loss and loose clamps. Exact boot-replacement steps depend on the shaft/joint design; no K4M-specific boot procedure was verified in the fetched pages.
safety: Support the vehicle securely and protect the gearbox output seal from shaft damage.
Do not allow the driveshaft to hang from the inner joint.

parts.name: CV boot kit and clamps
parts.notes: Confirm inner/outer joint type and boot kit against the VIN.

parts.name: Driveshaft nut
parts.notes: Use the part maker's replacement instruction.

removal.text: Inspect both inner and outer boots for tears, grease spray or loose clamps. For shaft removal, separate the hub/knuckle connection using the vehicle-specific driveshaft procedure and support the shaft at the inner joint.
Remove the shaft and joint only with the correct model-specific procedure; retain joint components in order and avoid contaminating the grease.

installation.text: Pack the joint with the specified grease, fit the correct boot and clamps with dedicated clamp tooling, and reassemble without twisting or pinching the boot.
Refit the shaft using the vehicle-specific axle-nut and gearbox-seal instructions; verify no fluid leak or boot contact through suspension travel.

checks: Check for grease leakage and confirm the boot folds do not bind at full steering lock or suspension travel.
After road-testing, inspect the gearbox seal and hub joint for leaks or noise.

faults.causes: Worn outer CV joint, often after boot damage and grease loss.

faults.symptom: Grease around wheel arch or subframe
faults.causes: Split CV boot or failed clamp.

name: Steering rack gaiter
summary: The rack gaiter protects the inner steering joint and rack from water and dirt. K4M-specific replacement torque data and a verified repair procedure were not found in the fetched sources.
safety: Support the vehicle securely and keep dirt away from the exposed rack shaft.
Wheel alignment must be checked after disturbing steering linkage length.

parts.name: Steering rack gaiter and clamps
parts.notes: Match the boot and clamp design to the rack fitted to the vehicle.

torques.notes: No verified torque value found; use the rack/boot maker's fitting method.

specs.label: Rack gaiter-specific procedure
specs.notes: No exact rack-gaiter procedure or boot dimensions were verified for this vehicle in fetched pages.

removal.text: Clean the steering linkage before opening the boot. Remove the outer track-rod end only if needed for access, recording the initial position as an assembly aid.
Release the gaiter clamps and slide the old boot off without scratching the rack shaft or allowing dirt into the rack.

installation.text: Inspect the rack shaft and inner joint, install the matching boot and clamps using the component maker's fitting instructions, and ensure the boot is not twisted.
Refit any removed steering joint, tighten to the verified applicable specification and obtain a wheel-alignment check.

checks: Inspect gaiter for splits, loose ends and trapped moisture.
Turn the steering lock-to-lock and confirm the boot flexes without twisting or pulling off.

faults.causes: Torn gaiter allowing contamination or rack fluid leak.
Inner joint, rack or bearing damage after gaiter failure.

name: Rear axle beam bushes (elastic mountings)
summary: Renault repair data documents replacement of the rear axle beam elastic mountings. The procedure applies to body variants B84, C84 or S84; verify the vehicle code before use.
safety: The rear axle is heavy and can destabilize the vehicle; strap the vehicle securely to the lift and support the axle beam with dedicated equipment.
Never support or lift the vehicle by the rear axle beam.
Keep the axle at the specified installation position while tightening the bushes.
tools: Press suitable for the mounting bushes

removal.text: Secure the vehicle to the lift with safety straps and support the rear axle beam using the specified fixture. Remove the lower damper mountings as required to position the axle assembly.
Release the elastic-mounting fasteners and lower or reposition the axle beam only enough to remove the mountings, preserving their orientation.

installation.text: Install the new mountings in the correct orientation. Set the distance between the body-side and axle-side damper mounting points to the documented setup dimension before tightening the mounting bolts.
Restore the brake hoses, ABS connectors, parking-brake cables and dampers according to their respective procedures; check alignment and brake operation.

checks: Confirm vehicle body code is within the stated applicability.
Verify mounting centring and specified axle position before final tightening.
Inspect brake pipes, ABS wiring, spring seats and damper mounts after assembly.

faults.symptom: Rear axle clunk or lateral movement
faults.causes: Deteriorated elastic mountings or loose axle fasteners.

faults.symptom: Rear alignment or tyre wear issue
faults.causes: Damaged axle mounting, bent beam or incorrect reinstallation position.
